QUIC packet fuzz target with custom decrypt, mutate, and reencrypt logic.

# Purpose
`fuzz_quic_wire` is a libFuzzer target for `fd_quic` packet processing. It builds a small QUIC instance, creates a dummy connection, and sends fuzz input as the payload of a synthetic UDP datagram through `fd_quic_process_packet`. The file sets up the fuzzer runtime in [`LLVMFuzzerInitialize`](<#llvmfuzzerinitialize>), disables normal logging, and uses a no-op `fd_aio` transmit callback so packet handling can run without real network output. After each input, it drives the QUIC service timers and checks packet, ACK, timeout, and connection cleanup paths. This target focuses on early QUIC wire handling, such as packet header parse, connection creation, retry handling, and service scheduling.

The file also defines a custom mutator for encrypted QUIC traffic. Helper functions such as [`guess_packet_size`](<#guess_packet_size>), [`decrypt_packet`](<#decrypt_packet>), [`decrypt_payload`](<#decrypt_payload>), [`encrypt_packet`](<#encrypt_packet>), and [`encrypt_payload`](<#encrypt_payload>) remove packet protection before mutation and restore it after mutation. This lets libFuzzer mutate decrypted QUIC packet contents while still feeding encrypted UDP datagrams to the parser. The code supports both long-header and short-header packets, and it uses fixed test keys for packet protection and header protection during fuzzing.
